name: q31-earliest-store-is-working
source:
let x = "s"
x = 1
exit
why: the working kind is the earliest store by source position; the later integer is the conflict (reported at stage 4)

name: q31-earliest-of-two-later-stores
source:
let x = 1
x = "s"
x = true
exit
why: integer first by position; string and boolean are conflicts

name: q31r-written-type-is-the-reference
source:
let x: string = "s"
x = 1
exit
why: a written type is the declaration's reference; the integer store is the conflict

name: q31r-initializer-before-an-earlier-site
source:
let a = 1
let x = "s"
x = a
exit
why: the let's initializer is the declaration whatever the position of the value copied into it later

name: q31r-list-literal-elements-are-the-declaration
source:
let xs = [1, 2]
xs.add("s")
exit
why: for list elements the declaration is the values in the literal; the text store is the error

name: q32a-unknown-after-known-is-held
source:
let x = 1
x = fromJson("1", default: 1)
exit
why: a value the compiler cannot know entering a decided place keeps the runtime check, whatever the order

name: q32a-unknown-before-known-is-held
why: order-free: the same mark when the unknown value comes first

name: q32a-null-default-stays-allowed
source:
let x = null
x = fromJson("1", default: null)
x = 1
exit
why: the owner: `fromJson(..., default: null)` stays allowed beside `let x = null`, `x = 1`; x is integer or null, checked at runtime

name: q32b-known-store-decides
source:
let x = hostValue
x = 1
exit
why: a known store decides a place with an unknown initializer; the host's value keeps the runtime check

name: q32c-null-default-in-a-literal-is-optionality
source:
let ys = [fromJson("t", default: null), 1]
exit
why: Q3.2b in aggregates with the owner's refinement: a known `default: null` contributes optionality to the element

name: q34-read-of-a-certainly-empty-list
source:
let xs = []
let n = xs.first
exit
why: reading the first element of a certainly empty list is a compile error; the read has no value

name: q34-read-of-a-maybe-empty-list-keeps-the-runtime-check
source:
let xs = []
xs.add(1)
let n = xs.first
exit
why: where the list may be empty the read keeps today's runtime check and has the element's type

name: q34-certainly-missing-property
why: a property the object certainly lacks: a compile error, the read has no value

name: q35-late-null-makes-optional
source:
let x = 1
x = null
exit
why: a late null makes the place optional

name: q35-late-null-in-an-element
source:
let xs = [1]
xs.add(null)
exit
why: the same in a part

name: q37-mixed-literal-earliest-kind
source:
let ys = [1, "a"]
let n = ys.first
exit
why: a mixed literal keeps TSV044 and the earliest member's kind is the working kind, so later uses are checked; the read of the element carries the same families (the report belongs to the literal)

name: q37-mixed-concatenation
source:
let ys = [1] + ["x"]
exit
why: the orchestrator's scope under Q3.7: a collection built from mixed kinds by `+` takes the earliest operand's kind

name: q38-no-automatic-union
source:
let x = 1
x = fromBase64("YQ==", default: 1)
exit
why: a union that does not fit the working kind is reported at the store; the place stays integer

name: q38-defined-union-first-then-fits
why: the reverse order compiles: the contract's union is the working union and the integer fits it

name: q38-written-union-admits-its-members
source:
let x: integer | string = 1
x = "s"
exit
why: several types in one variable are the author's deliberate act: the written union admits both

name: option-b-conflicting-property-across-literals
source:
let xs = [{a: 1}, {a: "x"}]
exit
why: the owner's option B: property `a` conflicts, the compile error names both values, the earliest kind counts; not a union of two shapes

name: option-b-different-property-sets-are-one-record
source:
let xs = [{x: 1}, {y: "a"}]
let n = xs.first.x
exit
why: different property sets are one record; a read of a property some literal lacks keeps the runtime presence check

name: option-b-reassigned-object-literals
why: two literals of one place are one schema; the conflicting property keeps the earliest kind

name: copy-takes-the-written-type
source:
let a: integer | string = 1
let b = a
b = "s"
exit
why: the owner, 2026-10-18: a copy of a variable with a written type takes that type, so `b = "s"` fits

name: b1-written-union-of-two-collections
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = hostValue
exit
why: each member of a written union keeps its own structure (Dropje97's B1); the host's value is held (Q3.2a)

name: b1-written-union-of-two-lists
source:
let v: integer[] | string[] = hostValue
exit
why: two lists stay two lists, not one list of a union

name: b2-file-order-decides-not-offsets

files.source:
global x = null
x = [1].get(0, default: "s")
exit

why: the second file's store at offset zero does not outrank the first file's defining store (ADR 0021 §1.6, Dropje97's B2a)

name: b2-same-offset-in-two-files-are-two-sites

files.source:
global x = null
x = [1].get(0, default: "s")
exit

why: two `get` expressions at one file-local offset are two defining sites; the boolean is the conflict (Dropje97's B2b), the export the working union

name: q39-method-on-every-member
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = hostValue
let n = v.length
exit
why: a method or property on a union must exist on every member (ADR 3): `length` exists on a list and a set, so the read is valid on both and has one kind

name: q39-method-missing-on-a-member
source:
let v: integer[] | string = hostValue
let n = v.first
exit
why: `first` exists on the list but not on the text: the read is invalid for the text member of the written union (one of the three combinations asked: both members and the host's dynamic view), which the operation's status records for stage 4's report

name: copy-of-a-written-collection-union-keeps-both
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = [1]
let a = v
exit
why: the copy takes the written type, not the initializer's list (PR review r4-B2); no conflict

name: copy-of-a-written-union-accepts-a-member-store
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = [1]
let a = v
a = ["s"].toSet()
exit
why: a later store of the other member fits the copied written type

name: copy-of-a-written-union-excludes-out-of-bound-evidence
source:
let a: integer | string = fromJson("1", default: null)
let b = a
b = "s"
exit
why: the copy takes the written `integer | string` and the held mark (Q3.2a); the initializer's null, outside the bound, is not the copy's evidence

name: b2-two-files-equal-offsets-are-two-bindings
why: two `let x` at offset 0:9 in two files are two bindings; main.tease's is held, other.tease's is not (see the differential's mutation test for the ledger's side)

name: b1-rebuilt-collection-keeps-the-members-apart
why: a collection rebuilt from a written union's member keeps that member's structure (§3.5: a permitted union's members stay their own; Sol's r4-B3): never a list of strings or a set of integers

name: w2-rebuilt-list-by-concatenation-keeps-the-members-apart
source:
let xs: integer[] | string[] = [1]
let ys = xs + []
let zs: integer[] | string[] = ys
exit
why: a list rebuilt by `+` from a written union's member keeps that member's structure, like the set operations (§3.5: one structure in, one out; Dropje97's W2-B1): never a list of both

name: w2-rebuilt-collection-of-a-written-union-element-stays-one
source:
let xs: (integer | string)[] = [1]
let ys = xs.toSet()
let zs: (integer | string) set = ys
exit
why: one written structure in, one out: a list whose written element is a union rebuilds into one set of that union, not into a set per element alternative (the r4 repair's over-split, Dropje97's W2 control)

name: q39-get-on-a-member-without-get
why: `get` exists on the list but not on the set: the read is invalid for the set member (one of the two combinations), the result is the list's element with the default (Q2); the written-union matrix found the `get` constraint answering for every structural member

name: q39-get-on-a-null-receiver
why: null has no `get`: the one combination is invalid, as `.first` on null is; the default is the get's own value (Q2), so the result is the integer (Astra's r5-B6)

name: q39-get-counts-the-null-alternative
source:
let a = null
a = [1]
let b = a.get(0, default: null)
exit
why: the early null makes the place optional (Q3.5); the null alternative has no `get`, the list has: one of two combinations invalid, as `.first` counts (Astra's r5-B6)

name: q39-get-does-not-count-a-cascade
source:
let a = [1]
a = "s"
let b = a.get(0, default: null)
exit
why: the text store is the conflict (Q3.1); a combination over a non-working alternative is a cascade and is not counted (§3.5), so the `get` has no status, as `.first` on the same receiver has none (Astra's r5-B6, Sol's r5-S1)

name: q39-get-with-a-key-without-evidence
source:
let xs = []
let k = xs.first
let a: integer[] | string set = [1]
let r = a.get(k, default: null)
exit
why: the key is a strict operand without evidence (the first of a list empty by construction, Q3.4): the get asks nothing and counts nothing (§3.5; Sol's r5-S1)

name: i1-feedback-rebuild-of-a-written-union-stays-finite
source:
let a: integer[] | string[] = [1]
a = a + []
exit
why: a rebuilt collection's case is the set of base cases it is built from, so a feedback edge returns to the same case: a finite fixpoint keeping both members (Sol's r5-B1, Astra's r5-B1)

name: i1-feedback-rebuild-of-a-permitted-union-stays-finite
why: the same with a permitted union from `get` (Sol's r5-B1): the two members of one type export as one text

name: i1-equal-shape-members-stay-apart
why: two permitted members of one object shape are two cases: the rebuild keeps them apart, no conflict between their properties (Astra's r5-B1)

name: copy-of-a-written-bound-with-a-permitted-initializer
source:
let a: integer[] | string set = [[1]].get(0, default: [2])
let b = a
let r = b.first
exit
why: the copy takes the written type by positive selection: the initializer's permitted members are not the copy's evidence whatever their role (Sol's r5-B2, Astra's r5-B2)

name: w3-permitted-projection-of-a-get-union
why: a part read through a permitted member is a member of the same union (Dropje97's W3-B1): the default may be of another type (V30 §16, §40), so `first` of either list is permitted, no conflict

name: w3-permitted-projection-of-a-property
why: the property of the object `get` chose is permitted as the object is

name: w3-permitted-projection-through-a-loop
why: the element a loop takes from the list a default admitted is permitted as the list is

name: w3-permitted-projection-after-a-rebuild
source:
let v = [[1]].get(0, default: ["s"])
let w = v + []
let n = w.first
exit
why: a rebuild keeps the members and their permission; the read through the rebuilt member is permitted

name: w3-permitted-projection-of-an-otherwise-union
source:
let v = [1] otherwise ["s"]
let n = v.first
exit
why: `otherwise` defines a permitted union as `get` with a default does

name: w3-mixed-literal-still-conflicts
source:
let v = [1, "s"]
let n = v.first
exit
why: a mixed literal is one witness, not a permitted union: its elements conflict and the earliest kind works (Q3.7); the control that W3-B1's repair must not change

name: fold-status-names-the-text-argument
source:
let a = 1
let b = "s"
let r = min(a, b, a)
exit
why: the owner (2026-10-19, B): when some combinations of a min or max call's arguments are invalid, the status names the arguments that can be invalid, counting nothing; a text cannot be ordered, so argument 2 is named; no combination is valid, so the call has no value

name: fold-status-names-both-of-an-unorderable-pair
source:
let a = 1
let b = 90 deg
let r = min(a, b)
exit
why: an integer and an angle are each orderable but not together: both arguments are named

name: fold-status-by-position-whatever-the-order
source:
let i = 1
let s = "s"
let a = i
a = s
let b = s
b = i
let r = min(b, a)
exit
why: `a` works as an integer and `b` as a text (Q3.1); the text argument is named by its position, here the first (Astra's r5-B5: the status must not depend on the order of the call)

name: fold-status-of-a-valid-call-is-none
why: every argument can be ordered with every other: no status; integer beside number widens to number

name: q2-default-types-the-get-alone
why: Q2 (the owner, 2026-10-17, A): the `default:` of a `get` types only that get's result, joined with the element; an empty list stays empty by construction, its element is not typed by the default (Astra's r5-N1 asked for the independent case)
